description:
Judge whether a gross salary offer in Germany is below, in or above the market, the way JobJump's offer check on jobjump.net does. Use it when the user names an offer amount for a role and asks whether it is fair, low or good, or how much to negotiate. Give the occupation in the user's own words in `job_title`, the gross amount in `offer_amount_eur` with `offer_period`, and the career stage in `seniority` when the user said it.

The offer is compared with JobJump's salary benchmark for the occupation and career stage – the same annual gross figures get_salary_benchmark returns as JobJump series. When `search_region` names one of 16 large German cities, JobJump's city salary factor for that city adjusts the benchmark; any other place is compared with the national figure and the response says so. An offer 8 percent or more under the benchmark is below market, 8 percent or more over it is above market, anything in between is in market. The response also gives the usual market corridor and a negotiation target range, all in annual gross euros.

The tool compares gross pay only and gives no tax or take-home figure; call calculate_net_salary with the offered amount for net pay. It is an orientation from aggregate data, not advice on a specific contract.

job_title.description: Occupation or job title of the offer in the user's own words, German or English. Gendered German forms are normalised, e.g. 'Erzieherin' resolves like 'Erzieher'.

offer_amount_eur.description: The offered gross pay in euros, before any deduction.

offer_period.description: Whether offer_amount_eur is an annual or a monthly figure. A monthly figure is multiplied by 12.

search_region.description: The German city where the job is, only if the user named one. Used solely for JobJump's city salary factor, which exists for 16 large cities; any other place gets no adjustment and the response says so. Never infer it, never pass coordinates.

seniority.description: Career stage of the person receiving the offer. 'entry' is JobJump's junior band, 'professional' its mid-level band, 'senior' its senior band, 'lead' its manager band.

name: evaluate_salary_offer

benchmark_eur_per_year.description: The value the offer is compared with: the national benchmark after the city factor.

city_factor_percent.description: JobJump city salary factor applied to the national benchmark, or null when none was applied.

city_factor_series_id.description: Provenance key of the city factor, or null when none was applied.

gap_percent.description: Offer minus benchmark, as a whole percentage of the benchmark. Negative means the offer is below it.

market_range.description: Usual market corridor: 6 percent either side of the benchmark.

target_range.description: Negotiation target: 2 to 10 percent above the benchmark.

verdict.description: below_market when the offer is 8 percent or more under the benchmark, above_market when 8 percent or more over it, in_market otherwise.

as_of.description: Vintage or reference period as published: 'YYYY', 'YYYY-MM' or an ISO date.

basis.description: Whether amounts are gross, net, or not a money amount.

dataset.description: Name of the dataset, e.g. 'Entgeltatlas' or 'JobJump salary aggregate'.

estimated.description: True when JobJump modelled or derived the value rather than observing or receiving it.

label.description: Short English name of what this series measures.

license.description: Licence or terms of use that apply to redistributing this series.

methodology_url.description: Public page describing how the series is produced, or null.

population.description: Who or what is counted, e.g. 'full-time employees subject to social insurance'.

sample_size.description: Number of underlying observations where JobJump knows it, otherwise null.

series_id.description: Stable key that series and values in this response refer to.

statistic.description: The statistic these values are. Read this before calling a value a median, a percentile or a maximum.

unit.description: Unit of every value carrying this series_id.

ags.description: Official German Kreis key (AGS) when one applies, otherwise null. Public administrative code, not a coordinate.

kind.description: Granularity the free-text input resolved to.

label.description: Coarse public name of the resolved region.

matched_input.description: The search_region text this resolution came from, echoed back so the user can see what was interpreted.

title: Evaluate a salary offer
